Xenoblade Chronicles X is the first game in the Xeno series to offer additional downloadable content. Paid downloadable content was made available for the Japanese version of the game, featuring new playable characters, Missions, and Skells, among others. This content was included with international releases of the game for free. Additionally, free data packs were made available, reducing load times for physical versions of the game.

As a series with much emphasis on plot and story-and-gameplay integration, the Xeno series has a notable amount of missable content. There are three varieties of content that can be considered within the umbrella of "missable": * Missable content can only be seen before certain story events, after which they are gone forever in that playthrough. For example, if an area becomes unrevisitable, any discoverable locations in that area are missable. * Mutually-exclusive content comes in groups for which the player makes a choice (intentionally or not) which one to see, with the others being unavailable in that playthrough. Li Garte Prison Camp refurbishment is a series of exchanges in Xenoblade Chronicles 3 taking place after the Prison Refurbishment is completed. The party pays Wheelideeli in several instalments to liven up the interior of Li Garte Prison Camp. In total, 500,000G must be paid to fully complete the refurbishment. Five levels of refurbishment are performed: * Level 1 costs 50,000G. It adds piles of supplies to the Central Cell along with a Fabricator at the Perimeter Outlet and a container in the Central Cell. * Level 2 costs 70,000G. The Maturation Process is an event in Xenoblade Chronicles 3 that acts as the Ascension Quest for both the Flash Fencer and Seraph es. As with regular Ascension Quests, it requires someone in the main party to be rank 10 in the applicable class - in this case it means both classes require someone to be rank 10 (they do not have to be the same person) - and for the applicable hero to be in the party, in this case Cammuravi. It can be triggered by opening the inner door to the lab with the Cradle within Colony Omega. Masahiro Iwamoto is a Japanese video game level designer and planner. He joined Monolith Soft in 2008 after graduating from a vocational school and has worked on the Xenoblade series as a level designer since. He took a bigger role in Future Connected and Future Redeemed, where he wrote the Ponspector's story arc scenario and then worked as the game director respectively.
